description: Downburst Effect on Transmission Towers is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Amal Elawady, Florida International University (fiu.edu). It's an aerodynamic testing of sectional models for a standalone transmission tower. The transmission tower is a steel-lattice-type cat-head overhead tower commonly incorporated in 110 kV, 150 kV, 220 kV, and 500 kV transmission lines. It has a height of 59.75m (196ft) with a square-shaped base of 13m (42.65ft), comprising four legs. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: downburst winds, aerodynamic testing, drag coefficient. Published 2024-12-02. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
